title: Week 4
description: The embryo implants in the uterine lining. The neural tube begins forming.
tips: Start taking folic acid if you haven't already.
Avoid alcohol and smoking.

title: Week 8
description: Baby has a heartbeat! Fingers and toes are beginning to form.
tips: Schedule your first prenatal appointment.
Stay hydrated and eat small frequent meals.

title: Week 12
description: End of the first trimester. Risk of miscarriage decreases significantly.
tips: First trimester screening tests are usually done this week.
You may start to feel more energetic.

title: Week 16
description: Baby can make facial expressions. You might start feeling movement soon.
tips: Consider starting prenatal yoga.
Discuss genetic testing options with your doctor.

title: Week 20
description: Halfway there! The anatomy scan is usually done around this week.
tips: Anatomy ultrasound can reveal the baby's sex if you want to know.
Sleep on your side for better circulation.

title: Week 24
description: Baby's lungs are developing. Movements are stronger and more frequent.
tips: Start counting kicks — aim for 10 movements in 2 hours.
Glucose screening test is typically done at 24–28 weeks.

title: Week 28
description: Third trimester begins. Baby can open and close eyes.
tips: Discuss birth plan options with your midwife or doctor.
Practice pelvic floor exercises.

title: Week 32
description: Baby is practicing breathing movements. Most organs are fully developed.
tips: Prepare your hospital bag.
Braxton Hicks contractions may become more noticeable.

title: Week 36
description: Baby is settling into a head-down position. Almost full term!
tips: Attend weekly prenatal check-ups.
Learn the signs of labour.

title: Week 40
description: Due date week! Baby is ready to meet you.
tips: Stay calm — only 5% of babies arrive on their due date.
Contact your doctor if contractions are 5 minutes apart or your water breaks.
